topSignals.title: Oracle Project Jupiter: Hearing examiner reverses dismissal threat — September 14 hearing confirmed to proceed
topSignals.text: — NMED hearing examiner Max Shepherd reversed his August 5 order (which had required developer Yucca Growth Infrastructure to brief a dismiss motion) and instead ruled the natural gas pipeline question will be argued at the full September 14 public hearing in Sunland Park, NM. The reversal lifts the immediate risk of outright dismissal and keeps the 2.45 GW Bloom SOFC air-quality permit application alive. New Energy Economy has sought reconsideration; the hearing will nonetheless be the decisive venue. Project Jupiter remains ~16% of total announced SOFC AI datacenter capacity. ABQ Journal

topSignals.title: FERC RM26-4: T-5 days to August 17 tariff-reform hard deadline
topSignals.text: — No compliance filings confirmed as of August 12. PJM, MISO, NYISO, and SPP all face binding "revise or justify" orders with a hard August 17 deadline. When filed, these submissions define the new large-load interconnection cost structure across ~70% of US load — directly determining the $5-20/MWh avoided-transmission-cost input that makes on-site SOFC economics compelling. CAISO is tracking a November filing; ISO-NE's "Bring Your Own Generation" (BYOG) mandate for new large-load data centers remains pending. FERC RM26-4 | Akin Gump

topSignals.title: Research: WashU Nature Nanotechnology PEM catalyst achieves ~25,000h estimated lifetime
topSignals.text: — Gao et al. (Washington University in St. Louis, with Brookhaven and Lawrence Berkeley NL), published August 6, 2026 (DOI: 10.1038/s41565-026-02244-8). Radial nanochannel carbon support enables Pt-Co intermetallic nanoparticles <5 nm at 1,000 degC anneal, retaining 85% performance after 150,000 severe voltage cycles. While this is a PEMFC result, not SOFC, the 25,000h lifetime estimate and ultra-low Pt loading advance the general case for fuel cell durability in data center applications; IP filed through WashU OTM. ScienceDaily

items.text: Elcogen (priority): Quiet day August 12. Status unchanged: E3000 G2 (>75% FC electrical efficiency, 90% with heat recovery, 23,000 SOEC rapid-cycle validated); ELCO I Tallinn factory (360 MW/yr) in volume production. Most recent moves: JNK India MoU (Feb 2026) and Southeast Asia Bonicorn/Eltronic Pt X partnership (Apr 2026). No new announcements today. Elcogen

Topsoe (priority): Quiet day August 12. Status unchanged: Herning SOEC factory (500 MW/yr) hibernated pending H2 demand recovery; First Ammonia supply deal terminated March 2026 after missed milestones; CEO Elena Scaltritti since June 1, 2026; FY2026 guidance DKK 7,600-8,400M. SOFC/data-center pathway deferred to 2029+. No new SOFC product or partnership announcements. Topsoe

Other players: Quiet day. Delta Electronics Q4 2026 Ceres Endura (10.8 kW) production ramp remains the nearest-term European-licensed SOFC commercialization milestone. Ceres Power + Centrica multi-GW on-site SOFC partnership (March 2026) unchanged. No new announcements from FuelCell Energy, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, or Aisin.

Oracle Project Jupiter (2.45 GW Bloom SOFC, Santa Teresa NM): Dismissal risk lifted — see Top Signal #1. September 14 public hearing is now the decisive date; pipeline access (twice-denied Energy Transfer route through state trust land) remains the central unresolved issue. If the hearing officer ultimately rules in favour of the applicant on the pipeline merits, the permit could clear and construction proceed. ABQ Journal

Hedgehog USA Texas (1.5 GW Bloom, Phase 1: 104 MW): No new filings or press releases beyond August 11 first appearance (TCEQ air-standard-permit registration, 4,615 ES-6.5 server blocks, phased ramp 104 MW -> 300 MW -> 800 MW -> 1.5 GW). ERCOT Batch Zero self-supply pathway exempts from FERC queue. Pre-construction status.

Active pipeline carry-forward: Crusoe/Cheyenne (900 MW Phase 1, first data halls H2 2026); FCEL/Fit Energy (380 MW total, 30 MW initial delivery H2 2026); Equinix >100 MW (19+ DCs); Bloom/Brookfield $25B EaaS framework; Nebius 328 MW EaaS; ECL/PowerCell 300 MW+ H2 partnership (Jul 14, Bosch-backed); MiTAC Fremont AI campus islanded microgrid.

FERC RM26-4 — T-5 days to August 17 hard deadline: See Top Signal #2. No tariff filings as of August 12. Recap: PJM/MISO/NYISO/SPP direct orders (August 8); CAISO November compliance target; ISO-NE BYOG mandate pending. August 17 remains the single most important near-term date for US on-site SOFC LCOE economics.

Background unchanged: NY EO 62 data center moratorium (50 MW+, islanded exemption active); Germany EnEfG PUE <=1.2/ERF >=10%/15% waste heat reuse from July 2026; EU CADA energy efficiency rating scheme delayed; ITC 48E 30% credit active for all fuel cell feedstocks; ERCOT Batch Zero self-supply active; 8 US states with enacted data center tax restrictions (OH, AZ, IL, NC, NJ, OK highlighted — see 08-11 entry).

Rolls-Royce SMR (UK): GDA Step 3 expected completion August 2026 — Rolls-Royce SMR is at Step 3 of the UK Office for Nuclear Regulation Generic Design Assessment; projected completion was August 2026. If confirmed, this marks a regulatory milestone for the UK market and could attract European data center developer interest. No formal ONR announcement confirmed today. Relevant as SOFC's primary long-horizon competition in European co-location markets.

Background unchanged: 13 US hyperscaler nuclear deals totalling >9.8 GW; Terrestrial Energy + Riot Platforms 4,000 MW (May 2026); Meta three-company nuclear deal (Jan 2026). Nuclear 10+ year lead times remain the primary SOFC competitive differentiator for near-term deployment.

Bloom Energy (BE): Stock ~$345.85 (+250% YTD as of early August). Q2 2026 (released Jul 29): record $1.065B revenue (+166% YoY, first >$1B quarter); net income $196.3M; gross margin 33.4%; FY2026 guidance raised to $3.9-4.2B (was $3.4-3.8B after Q1). Product backlog ~$6B; total contracted backlog ~$20B. Ongoing: Hunterbrook Media "Bloom's Big Lie" (Jul 8) scandium supply chain investigation + federal securities class action lawsuit; Bloom denies all claims. Analysts remain broadly bullish (Evercore "AI Reach Is Deeper Than Investors Thought," Aug 7). Quiet day August 12 for new announcements.
Other players: Quiet day. No new material financial disclosures from FuelCell Energy, Ceres Power, or SolydEra.

Nature Nanotechnology (Aug 6, 2026) — Pt-Co intermetallic PEM catalyst, 25,000h estimated lifetime (Gao et al., WashU + Brookhaven + LBL + Northeastern + U Pittsburgh; DOI: 10.1038/s41565-026-02244-8): Radial nanochannel carbon support enables dense, evenly distributed Pt-Co nanoparticles <5 nm at 1,000 degC anneal. 85% performance retention after 150,000 severe voltage cycles (~25,000h). Key: overcomes the activity-stability tradeoff in intermetallic catalysts. PEMFC-focused but benchmarks fuel cell durability expectations broadly. IP filed through WashU OTM. ScienceDaily

Two MS-SOFC comprehensive reviews (Springer, 2026): (1) "A comprehensive review on the progress and evaluation of metal supported solid oxide fuel cells (MS-SOFC)" — Journal of Solid State Electrochemistry 2026, DOI: 10.1007/s10008-026-06571-7: covers rapid start-up, thermal cycling tolerance, mechanical stability. (2) "Comprehensive review of current trends and future directions of metal-supported solid oxide fuel cell: From materials to applications" — IJMMM vol. 33, 2026, DOI: 10.1007/s12613-026-3402-0: systematic analysis from materials to system applications. Both confirm MS-SOFC cost and thermal-robustness improvements are narrowing the gap to ceramic SOFC at small-system scale. Springer MS-SOFC 1 | Springer MS-SOFC 2

[Applied Energy, 2025 — first citation] Reversible SOFC/SOEC 60-cell stack cycling, 4,000 h — "Analysis of electrochemical degradation phenomena of a 60-cell SOC stack operated in reversible SOFC/SOEC cycling mode" (ScienceDirect pii/S0306261925002958). SOFC degradation: -1.7%/kh; SOEC: +2.3%/kh; both dominated by ohmic resistance growth. SOFC initial electrical efficiency: 57% at 1,068 W rated power. Directly relevant for long-term degradation modeling in reversible SOC / power-to-X data center designs. LCOE-model relevant (degradation capex term). ScienceDirect

[NCBI/PMC — open-access special issue] "Materials Frontiers for Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCs): Structure-Performance Correlation" (PMC12693468): open-access editorial for a multi-paper special issue covering electrode microstructure-performance links, electrolyte thin-film advances, and interconnect materials. Cell/stack-materials focus; no system-level or LCOE content. Reference for stack-component tracking. NCBI PMC
No newly published (August 12) SOFC system-level papers found in arXiv, Nature, or major journal feeds today.

lcoe.text: [First citation] Modular SOFC system LCOE: $0.155/kWh at 1 GW scale — "Scalable modular design of solid oxide fuel cell systems for enhanced large-scale power generation" (Nature Communications, Feb 2026, DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-69110-y): 66.3% electrical efficiency; LCOE $0.155/kWh (= $155/MWh) for 1 GW modular system; degradation rate 0.2%/kh constant-power. NOTE: modeled case (likely Chinese cost basis); use as directional input only, cross-check against INOCEL capex assumptions. Nature Communications

[First citation] Reversible SOC stack degradation rates (Applied Energy, 2025): SOFC -1.7%/kh, SOEC +2.3%/kh over 4,000h cycling — useful for modeling degradation-driven capex replacement cycles in reversible SOC scenarios.

Background carry-forward: US natural gas $4.00-4.90/MMBtu (EIA 2026); SOFC commercial system capex $4,000-6,000/kW (target: $1,000/kW); CCGT $2,000-2,200/kW; solar+battery $25/MWh LCOE (unsuitable for 24/7 AI baseload).
